newsitem.title: USA: Ohio schools coalition proposes funding program.
newsitem.headline: Ohio schools coalition proposes funding program.

text.p: An Ohio schools coalition on Tuesday recommended dedicating state lottery proceeds to help address inadequacies in the public school funding system.
Most lottery proceeds should be used to back bonds for new school construction and major renovations, according to the Ohio Coalition for Equity and Adequacy of School Funding.

The coalition, which represents a number of school districts that successfully challenged the current state funding system, also recommended that the rest of the lottery funds go to building maintenance.
The Ohio Supreme Court last month overturned the state's school funding system, finding that it did not provide adequate funding to all students.
The justices gave state officials one year to overhaul the system. Gov. George Voinovich formed a task force to address the supreme court's concerns, which met for the second time on Monday.

Voinovich also asked the justices to reconsider the ruling and to clarify certain sections. The school districts that challenged the current state funding system have objected to the governor's requests, which remained pending before the supreme court on Tuesday.
The coalition also recommended setting per pupil funding at $3,900 for fiscal year 1998 and $4,400 for 1999 for students in regular classrooms in grades four through eight.
The state should also fund at least 60 percent of transportation costs, but now funds about 30 percent, according to the coalition.
The coalition report also recommended increasing the number of teacher training days and increasing the length of the school year.
A spokesman for the governor could not be reached immediately for comment on the coalition recommendations.
